title: Aft Sill Frame Web — Bonded and Bolted Insert Repair

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Permanent insert repair for cracking in the web of an aft sill frame, cutting the cracked web area out and replacing it with a bolted insert that carries the shear across the removed region.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the shear capability of an aft sill frame web after a crack has been removed, without replacing the complete frame rib.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the crack extent by detailed visual inspection and by an eddy current sweep of the whole web panel bounded by the frame flanges and the adjacent stiffeners. A crack that reaches either flange radius is outside the scope of this repair and needs an engineering assessment, because the flange is the primary load path and this repair does not restore it. Measure the distance from each crack tip to the nearest fastener and to the flange radius and record both. Where two cracks are present in one web panel, only the case where they are more than 60 mm apart is covered. Check the adjacent lower intercostal for a companion indication before the web is cut, because the two often crack together.
sections.repair_procedure: Support the frame with the local jack before any material is removed. Cut the cracked web area out to a rectangle with 20 mm corner radii, keeping at least 30 mm of parent web to each flange radius and to each stiffener. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the cut edge over its full length. Cut the insert from the material given on repair drawing RD-53-31-11-904 and drill it to the pattern shown, using the insert as a template on the parent web. Ream every hole and do an eddy current inspection of each reamed hole. Install the insert with a doubler strap on the inboard face, fastened with bolts AGS713311K3 and anchor nuts EN581282-4E to the torque given on the drawing. Where the insert reaches the frame rib D5331113688429 attachment row, use rivets EN545167-02 in the outer row instead of bolts. Apply the surface protection of ATA 51-20 to all new surfaces and seal the insert edge. Remove the local jack only after the fastening is complete.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 12 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of the insert perimeter and of both cut edges every 3 000 flight cycles, and a detailed visual inspection of the doubler strap at every C-check. Not more than two frames per aircraft may carry this repair at the same time. Report the repair to Aeralis with the crack length and the flight cycle count at the finding.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 25 mm in length that do not reach a flange radius and are not closer than 20 mm to a fastener centre. One crack per web panel, or two if they are more than 60 mm apart. Not more than two frames per aircraft.

repair_drawings.title: Bolted web insert, aft sill frame

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two bolted rows of 16 around the insert perimeter at 25 mm pitch, with a riveted outer row of 24 at 20 mm pitch where the insert meets the frame rib attachment
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 12 000 flight cycles; repeat eddy current inspection of the insert perimeter every 3 000 flight cycles.
